messages:
luis_cust: Hi, since yesterday our outbound connections to the Private control plane (cp-nyc.private.redwood.com) started failing during mTLS handshake. We see connection resets and 526-like errors from our proxy. Happened after corporate NGFW update. Can you help? (acct: acme-corp, tenant: acme-prod)

anna_devops: Sorry to hear — can you paste the exact error from your side? Any client logs or tcpdump? Did you rotate client certs recently?

luis_cust: Logs show "TLS handshake failure: handshake aborted by peer" and we see FIN immediately after ClientHello on the wire. No cert rotation on our side. NGFW pushed a policy change yesterday evening.

raj_eng: Sounds like a middlebox/SSL inspection issue. Can you run:
```
openssl s_client -connect cp-nyc.private.redwood.com:443 -servername cp-nyc.private.redwood.com -msg -tlsextdebug
```
and paste the output (feel free to redact cert blobs). Also what IPs does the hostname resolve to from your environment?

luis_cust: It resolves to 10.11.12.34 and 10.11.12.35. We see SYN/ACK then immediate RST. Ran openssl; no ServerHello returned — it just errors out with "read:errno=104". Uploaded pcap: https://files.acme/internal/pcaps/mtls-2026-03-16.pcap

elaine_sre: @raj_eng those IPs map to our control-plane frontends in the peering region. 10.11.12.35 is our interconnect address. A lot of customers needed to add our control plane addresses to egress allowlists after we changed NAT pools.

anna_devops: Also confirm whether the NGFW is doing TLS inspection / SSL forward proxy. If they are re-signing certs (man-in-the-middle), that will break mutual TLS because the client cert chain won't reach our servers.

luis_cust: They did enable SSL inspection and re-signing for a subset of traffic. How can I prove it's the proxy? Any quick checks?

raj_eng: Quick steps: 1) try curl with client certs and compare network trace; 2) capture ClientHello and verify key_share and SNI are intact. If the proxy strips key_share or rewrites SNI, the handshake fails. From our logs we see ClientHello arrive but then TLS session doesn't progress to CertificateRequest — consistent with a proxy terminating TLS.

luis_cust: Running now:
```
curl -v --cert client.pem --key client.key https://cp-nyc.private.redwood.com/healthz
```
Response: "empty reply from server". Packet capture shows ClientHello then TCP RST.

elaine_sre: Ok. Next steps for you and NGFW team: 1) Add an egress bypass (no TLS inspection) for the control plane endpoints (10.11.12.34/32, 10.11.12.35/32) on port 443; 2) If they can only do hostname-based bypass, ensure SNI passthrough is enabled and the proxy does not terminate TLS for cp-nyc.private.redwood.com; 3) Temporarily route a test host via a non-inspecting NAT to confirm. Share a redacted pcap and we will correlate against our ingress logs (we'll look around 1945127000 UTC).

support_bot: Ticket created: SUP-98421. Assigned to eng-sre. Initial response ETA 2h.

luis_cust: NGFW team says they can only bypass by FQDN, not IP. They asked for exact SNI/CN/SAN values to match. What should we provide?

raj_eng: SNI should be cp-nyc.private.redwood.com. Server cert SANs include cp-nyc.private.redwood.com and controlplane.internal.redwood.com. Ask them to match SNI to cp-nyc.private.redwood.com and to not terminate TLS for that hostname. Also ensure OCSP stapling passthrough — some proxies drop connections when OCSP responses are changed.

luis_cust: If they refuse hostname bypass, is there any alternate path? We can do VPN but that's heavy.

elaine_sre: As a fallback we can provision a temporary peered egress IP on our side and open it to your NAT for a limited maintenance window, but that requires infra changes and an ACL. Let's try hostname bypass first. Please update when NGFW tests the bypass (they said 14:30 PT). Post results and the pcap link; we'll correlate and re-open if needed.

anna_devops: One extra note: if their proxy supports SNI-based bypass, verify they are matching the raw SNI (not a rewritten host header) and that hostname passthrough is configured for TLS 1.2/1.3. Good luck :thumbsup:

luis_cust: Will update after the 14:30 test. Thanks everyone. (end)
